lines.text: Light crosses a kitchen: seventeen seconds.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt kɹˈɔsᵻz ɐ kˈɪtʃən: sˈɛvəntˌiːn sˈɛkəndz.

lines.text: Ten million times slower. One second now lasts about one hundred sixteen days. A hundred million times slower, and one second lasts more than three years. At this speed, a flash of light would take almost two seconds to cross the room. A billion times slower. One second now lasts about thirty-two years. Light moves about thirty centimeters in a billionth of a second. So at this speed, it crawls thirty centimeters in one second.
lines.phonemes: tˈɛn mˈɪliən tˈaɪmz slˈoʊɚ. wˈʌn sˈɛkənd nˈaʊ lˈæsts ɐbˌaʊt wˈʌn hˈʌndɹɪd sˈɪkstiːn dˈeɪz. ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd mˈɪliən tˈaɪmz slˈoʊɚ, ænd wˈʌn sˈɛkənd lˈæsts mˈɔːɹ ðɐn θɹˈiː jˈɪɹz. æt ðɪs spˈiːd, ɐ flˈæʃ ʌv lˈaɪt wʊd tˈeɪk ˈɔːlmoʊst tˈuː sˈɛkəndz tə kɹˈɔs ðə ɹˈuːm. ɐ bˈɪliən tˈaɪmz slˈoʊɚ. wˈʌn sˈɛkənd nˈaʊ lˈæsts ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾitˈuː jˈɪɹz. lˈaɪt mˈuːvz ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾi sˈɛntɪmˌiːɾɚz ɪn ɐ bˈɪliənθ əvə sˈɛkənd. sˌoʊ æt ðɪs spˈiːd, ɪt kɹˈɔːlz θˈɜːɾi sˈɛntɪmˌiːɾɚz ɪn wˈʌn sˈɛkənd.

lines.text: Someone flicks on a flashlight. A glowing front of light leaves the lens, and spreads across the room. Behind it, the table is lit. The drop of water above the cup hangs there, frozen. If you just replayed that in your head, tap like and follow. It takes about seventeen seconds for the light to reach the far wall. And in the corner, a computer chip is about to start ticking.
lines.phonemes: sˈʌmwʌn flˈɪks ˌɔn ɐ flˈæʃlaɪt. ɐ ɡlˈoʊɪŋ fɹˈʌnt ʌv lˈaɪt lˈiːvz ðə lˈɛnz, ænd spɹˈɛdz əkɹˌɑːs ðə ɹˈuːm. bᵻhˈaɪnd ɪt, ðə tˈeɪbəl ɪz lˈɪt. ðə dɹˈɑːp ʌv wˈɔːɾɚɹ əbˌʌv ðə kˈʌp hˈæŋz ðˈɛɹ, fɹˈoʊzən. ɪf juː dʒˈʌst ɹˈiːpleɪd ðæt ɪn jʊɹ hˈɛd, tˈæp lˈaɪk ænd fˈɑːloʊ. ɪt tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt sˈɛvəntˌiːn sˈɛkəndz fɚðə lˈaɪt tə ɹˈiːtʃ ðə fˈɑːɹ wˈɔːl. ænd ɪnðə kˈɔːɹnɚ, ɐ kəmpjˈuːɾɚ tʃˈɪp ɪz ɐbˌaʊt tə stˈɑːɹt tˈɪkɪŋ.
